title: When to see a vet
intro: Some signs mean home care is not enough. Here is when to rush to a vet, and when to book a visit soon.
note: This list comes from our 7 years of rescue experience and trusted veterinary sources. It is not a full list, and it never replaces a vet. When in doubt, always call your vet.
ask_title: Not sure if it is an emergency?
ask_body: Message us and tell us what you see. We will help you decide your next step, but if your cat seems in danger, go straight to a vet.

signs.title: Swollen ear flap
signs.body: A puffy, soft ear flap can be an ear hematoma, a pocket of blood under the skin. It needs a vet to drain or treat it.

signs.title: Yellow ears, gums or nose
signs.body: A yellow tint on the skin, gums or inside the ears can be jaundice, often a sign of a liver problem or another serious illness.

signs.title: Blood in the stool
signs.body: Blood in their poop, red or very dark, always needs to be checked by a vet.

signs.title: Not eating for 2 days
signs.body: A cat who stops eating for more than two days can quickly become very ill, especially their liver.

signs.title: Hiding and not eating
signs.body: Cats hide pain. If your cat is hiding and refusing food, something is wrong.

signs.title: Sore or infected eyes
signs.body: Never use any eye drops before a vet checks the eye. The wrong drops can damage the eye and even cause blindness.

signs.title: Straining but cannot pee
signs.body: Going back and forth to the litter box with only drops or no urine at all, often crying. Most common in male cats. A blocked cat can die within a day or two, so go straight to a vet.

signs.title: Trouble breathing
signs.body: Breathing with an open mouth, panting or gasping. Cats do not pant like dogs, so this is always urgent.

signs.title: Swallowed string or thread
signs.body: String, thread, wool, hair ties or tinsel. If you see a string hanging from the mouth or bottom, never pull it and do not try to make them vomit. Go to a vet.

signs.title: Swallowed something else
signs.body: Toys, needles, plastic or bones. Even if your cat seems fine, call your vet. Watch for vomiting, belly pain and not eating.

signs.title: Vomiting again and again
signs.body: Repeated vomiting, especially with weakness, not eating or pale gums.

signs.title: Pale or white gums
signs.body: Healthy gums are light pink. Pale, white or grey gums can mean blood loss or shock.

signs.title: Seizure or collapse
signs.body: Shaking fits, falling over, or a cat who is very weak and barely responds to you.

signs.title: A fall, accident or fight
signs.body: After a fall from height, a car accident or a bad fight, see a vet even if your cat is still walking. Some injuries are inside and cannot be seen.

signs.title: Heavy bleeding
signs.body: Bleeding that does not stop, from a wound, the mouth, the stool or the urine.

signs.title: Ate something poisonous
signs.body: Lilies, human medicines, cleaning products or rat poison. Go to the vet even before signs appear, and bring the package or plant with you.

signs.title: Heatstroke
signs.body: Panting, heavy drooling and a body that feels very hot, especially on hot days or after being shut in a car or room.

signs.title: Crying in pain
signs.body: Screaming or crying when touched, a hunched back, or a cat who suddenly cannot use their back legs.

signs.title: Yellow or brown teeth
signs.body: Tartar building up on the teeth. A vet can clean them (scaling) before it causes gum problems.

signs.title: Red, swollen or bleeding gums
signs.body: Inflamed gums can be painful and make eating hard.

signs.title: Bad breath
signs.body: A smelly mouth is often a sign of dental or gum disease, and sometimes of other illness.

signs.title: Drinking a lot of water
signs.body: A cat who suddenly drinks much more than usual can have kidney problems, diabetes or another illness.

signs.title: Losing a lot of fur
signs.body: Fur falling out in clumps, or bald patches.

signs.title: Scaly or crusty patches
signs.body: White, flaky patches on the skin, especially if they spread to more places. It can be a fungal infection.

signs.title: Black dirt in the ears
signs.body: Dark, crumbly dirt inside the ears is often ear mites.

signs.title: Tiny jumping bugs
signs.body: Small bugs moving and jumping in the fur are fleas. The whole home needs treating too.
